story.summary: Chinese AI model developers DeepSeek and MiniMax cleared initial pre-export registration hurdles under China's updated export rules. The approval permits open-source code sharing and global commercial licensing under international deployment frameworks.

draft.body:
Chinese artificial intelligence developers DeepSeek and MiniMax have completed the initial registration process required under Beijing's draft China AI export rules, enabling both companies to move forward with international commercial licensing and open-source distribution. The development was initially revealed on the evening of October 22, 2026, by Yuyuan Tantian, a social media account affiliated with state broadcaster China Central Television, and reported by [Pandaily](https://pandaily.com/deepseek-minimax-complete-ai-technology-export-registration-open-source-overseas-licensing).

The filings show that two leading model makers have now worked through the process in practice under China's proposed export management system for advanced artificial intelligence. The move confirms that leading Chinese AI model makers can continue international distribution under official regulatory oversight while Beijing formalizes broader rules governing the export of advanced computing tools.

## How China AI Export Rules Regulate Model Deployment

On October 16, 2026, China's Ministry of Commerce and the Ministry of Science and Technology published a draft revision of the Catalogue of Technologies Prohibited or Restricted From Export for public comment. As [The Edge Malaysia reported](https://theedgemalaysia.com/node/822972), the revisions have been under development since the first half of 2026 and incorporate feedback from research institutes and industry participants. The draft adds 23 AI-related items encompassing large language models, autonomous agents, computing clusters, and specialized information processing.

State media emphasized that the updated catalogue is intended to establish clear regulatory boundaries rather than impose an outright ban on artificial intelligence exports. The Ministry of Commerce clarified that the vast majority of AI technologies will remain freely exportable. Furthermore, registration under the system is distinct from a restrictive export ban, serving instead as a filing mechanism while the draft remains open for public consultation.

[[FIG1]]

## DeepSeek and MiniMax Put Rules Into Practice

Actions taken by DeepSeek and MiniMax illustrate how developers are navigating the compliance steps in practice. According to Huxiu, DeepSeek open-sourced its large-scale inference framework, DeepInfer, alongside a companion toolkit called deepseek-recipe on October 20, 2026.

MiniMax addressed overseas jurisdictions that were excluded under its earlier model licenses. As detailed by [Pandaily](https://pandaily.com/deepseek-minimax-complete-ai-technology-export-registration-open-source-overseas-licensing), MiniMax introduced a formal application mechanism for entities in regions such as the United States, the European Union, the United Kingdom, and South Korea. Under this structure, MiniMax keeps its model weights open, but overseas organizations in those regions must undergo a compliance review and secure a license before deploying the models on local infrastructure.

Neither DeepSeek nor MiniMax immediately replied to requests for comment regarding their filings, according to reporting from [Reuters via WHTC](https://whtc.com/2026/10/23/chinas-deepseek-minimax-win-approval-for-ai-global-use-state-media-affiliated-entity-says).

## Carveouts for Cloud APIs and Public Open-Source Code

The Ministry of Commerce established explicit carveouts that delineate which deployment formats trigger export scrutiny. Under the proposed rules, technologies that have entered the public domain through open-source code releases or published academic papers fall outside the scope of export restrictions entirely.

Regulators also drew distinctions based on delivery architecture:

- Providing model access through application programming interfaces (APIs), software-as-a-service (SaaS) platforms, web portals, mobile apps, or lightweight on-device runtimes does not constitute an export of large-model technology.
- Local deployment of a restricted model on overseas physical infrastructure falls directly under export management.
- Chinese companies running their own cloud infrastructure or data centers abroad, as well as conducting joint research with foreign resources, would qualify for automatic licensing described as export upon filing.

These exemptions allow international software developers to integrate Chinese AI backends via cloud APIs without encountering export control barriers.

[[FIG2]]

## Geopolitical Context and Market Reactions

The regulatory update arrives amid continued competition between Beijing and Washington over advanced technology. China previously updated its export control catalogue in 2020 to include algorithms after the Trump administration attempted to force a sale of TikTok's American operations. More recently, Beijing intervened to unwind Meta Platforms Inc.'s acquisition of Manus, an AI agent startup with Chinese origins, as noted by [The Edge Malaysia](https://theedgemalaysia.com/node/822972).

State media posts contrasted Beijing's approach with Washington's targeted export bans and technology blockades. As reported by [AsiaOne](https://www.asiaone.com/digital/chinas-deepseek-minimax-win-approval-ai-global-use-state-media-affiliated-entity-says), Yuyuan Tantian noted that overseas internet users had urged other Chinese open-source large language model developers to follow suit.

Industry analysts indicate that compliance clarity could influence global enterprise adoption. According to [VKTR](https://www.vktr.com/ai-market/deepseek-minimax-cleared-by-china-for-global-ai-rollout/), enterprise architectures are shifting toward multi-model systems where organizations evaluate models independently of country of origin, while IDC Research Director Tim Law noted that the future AI landscape will be varied with models of all types and sizes from different geographies.

faq.q: What approvals did DeepSeek and MiniMax receive?
faq.a: Both companies completed the required export registration under China's proposed AI export control catalogue, allowing them to proceed with open-source software distribution and authorized overseas commercial licensing.

faq.q: Are API calls and cloud services restricted under the new export rules?
faq.a: No. The Ministry of Commerce specified that serving models through cloud APIs, SaaS platforms, web interfaces, and lightweight on-device deployment does not count as exporting large-model technology.

faq.q: How does MiniMax handle model deployment in the US and Europe?
faq.a: MiniMax established a compliance route allowing users in previously excluded jurisdictions, including the US, EU, UK, and South Korea, to access open model weights while requiring a formal compliance review and license for local on-premises deployment.
